title: BA1/986/2021 of HARISH SINGH NAINWAL Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
First Bail Application No. 986 of 2021
Harish Singh Nainwal ...Applicant
Versus
State of Uttarakhand ....Respondent
Present:-
Mr. R.S. Sammal, Advocate for the applicant.
 Mr. Balwinder Singh, Brief Holder for the State.

Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
Applicant Harish Singh Nainwal, is in judicial custody in
FIR No.14 of 2021, under Section 376, 506 IPC and Section 3/4 of
Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (for short,
"the Act"), Police Station Kapkot, District Bageshwar. He has sought
his release on bail.
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties through video
conferencing and perused the record.
3. FIR in the instant case was lodged on 08.02.2021 under
Sections 376, 506 IPC by the victim herself. According to it, the
victim came in touch with the applicant through facebook and in due
course of time they became friends. The applicant promised to marry
the victim. On 12.07.2019, the applicant called the victim at
Bageshwar and there spiked her meal and committed rape upon her.
The applicant thereafter threatened the victim not to reveal this
incident to anyone and again assured to marry her. But subsequently,
he declined. These and other details are in the FIR.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant would submit that in
fact, the whole story is false. The applicant and the victim both were
friends. They married and this marriage was attended by the mother of
the victim. The marriage was solemnized in a temple. There are

2
photographs enclosed with the bail application. The girl is a major.
Her horoscope, which was given to the applicant by her only,
establishes this fact. The relations were consensual. The victim is
married wife of the applicant. The marriage was solemnized in the
month of November, 2020. It is argued that after marriage, there was
some dispute between the father of the victim and the father of the
applicant, therefore, false FIR is lodged. It is argued that it is a case fit
for bail.
5. Learned State counsel would submit that on the date of
incident, the victim was a minor; the date of birth as per school record
is 01.07.2002; during investigation, the applicant did not give any
evidence of their marriage.
6. At this stage, learned counsel for the applicant also
argued that the State has not denied the photographs or the factum of
the horoscope. The State did not deny that the applicant married the
victim.
7. It is the stage of bail. Much is not required to be
deliberated upon at this stage. The photographs show that the victim
was dressed as a bride, jewellery as well as vermillion on her
forehead. It is argued that mother of the victim is also seen in the
photographs, she was also agreeable to the marriage. The victim in her
statement has admitted this fact that she was in relations with the
applicant. The applicant had assured her to marry, but according to
her, subsequently, the applicant denied.
8. In the counter affidavit, the State has not stated anything
about the factum of marriage between the applicant and the victim as
stated by the applicant in his bail application.
9. Perhaps, all these issues would be raised and discussed
during trial. But, having considered all the attending factors, this Court
is of the view that this case is fit for bail.
10. Bail application is allowed.

3
11. Let the applicant Harish Singh Nainwal be released on
bail, on his executing a personal bond and furnishing two reliable
sureties, each of the like amount, to the satisfaction of the Court
concerned.
12. This bail order be forwarded to concerned Court as well
as the concerned jail through e-mail also.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 28.05.2021
Sanjay
